ReViT-RF: A hybrid ResNet-50–Vision Transformer with a Radiomic Feature Fusion framework for lung tumor classification and TNM-based stage prediction using CT images
nodes.venue: PLOS One
nodes.abstract: Lung cancer is one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, emphasizing the need for accurate, automated, and clinically interpretable diagnostic systems. Although existing deep learning (DL) models have achieved promising performance in classifying lung nodules as benign or malignant, most approaches are limited to binary classification and provide insufficient support for detailed tumor characterization and TNM staging. Furthermore, conventional convolutional neural networks (CNNs) are effective in extracting local morphological features but often fail to capture long-range spatial dependencies. In contrast, transformer-based models can learn global contextual information but may compromise fine-grained local feature representation. To address these limitations, this study proposes a hybrid ResNet-50–Vision Transformer with Radiomic Feature Fusion (ReViT-RF) framework for lung tumor classification and component-wise TNM stage prediction using thoracic computed tomography (CT) images from the publicly available Lung Image Database Consortium and Image Database Resource Initiative (LIDC-IDRI) dataset. The primary clinical objectives of the proposed framework are to: (i) classify pulmonary nodules as benign or malignant, and (ii) predict individual TNM components, including primary tumor extent (T), lymph node involvement (N), and metastatic status (M) for malignant cases. To improve tumor visibility and image quality, CT images are initially preprocessed using Contrast-Limited Adaptive Histogram Equalization (CLAHE) and intensity normalization. The proposed ReViT-RF architecture integrates the complementary advantages of ResNet-50 and Vision Transformer (ViT) for comprehensive feature learning. The CNN branch extracts local morphological, textural, and structural characteristics, whereas the transformer branch captures long-range spatial relationships and global contextual dependencies. In addition, handcrafted radiomic features, including shape, size, texture, and spatial descriptors, are fused with deep features to provide clinically meaningful information for accurate TNM component prediction. The dataset is divided into training, validation, and testing subsets using an 80:10:10 ratio, with data augmentation applied only to the training set to prevent information leakage. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework achieves an accuracy of 97.62% for benign–malignant classification, along with high precision, recall, and F1-score values. Moreover, independent prediction of TNM components provides detailed stage-related information rather than relying on a single aggregated stage label, enabling more precise tumor assessment and clinical decision support. Furthermore, explainability analysis using Gradient-weighted Class Activation Mapping (Grad-CAM) identifies the critical tumor regions contributing to model predictions, improving interpretability and enhancing clinician confidence. Overall, by combining hybrid deep feature extraction, radiomic feature fusion, component-wise TNM stage prediction, and explainable AI analysis, the proposed ReViT-RF framework provides a reliable, comprehensive, and clinically interpretable solution for automated lung tumor analysis.

nodes.name: Post-hoc reliability assessment and visual explanation for deep learning-based oral mucosal lesion detection
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Modern deep learning detectors for oral mucosal lesions produce class predictions and softmax confidence scores, but neither reveals which learned visual patterns supported the prediction nor whether it can be trusted. We developed a post-hoc method that, without modifying an already-trained YOLO detector, makes the basis of each prediction explicit through embedding-space analysis and provides a training-distribution-aware estimate of its reliability. Methods A YOLOv11 detector was trained on 3104 intraoral photographs covering oral lichen planus (OLP), proliferative verrucous leukoplakia (PVL)/leukoplakia and oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC), supplemented with 464 healthy mucosa images. For every detection, a feature embedding was extracted from the deepest backbone layer, projected to a 2-D manifold using supervised neighborhood component analysis (NCA) and unsupervised uniform manifold approximation and projection (UMAP), and scored against per-class kernel density estimates fitted on correctly predicted training samples. Density scores were compared with softmax confidence using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and nearest-neighbor retrieval in the embedding space provided visual explanations of individual predictions. Results Per-class detection F1-scores were 0.88 (OLP), 0.76 (PVL/Leukoplakia), 0.73 (OSCC) and 0.93 (healthy mucosa). Density-based ROC area-under-the-curve (AUC) values ranged from 0.92 to 0.95 across the four classes, with NCA slightly outperforming UMAP. The density score consistently identified low-confidence predictions that softmax did not flag, and the nearest-neighbor mosaic produced visually interpretable explanations of individual predictions. Conclusions Embedding-space density on a frozen YOLO detector provides an interpretable, post-hoc reliability measure for oral mucosal lesion detection. Combined with nearest-neighbor visual retrieval, it complements softmax confidence and supports post-hoc clinical audit without retraining.

nodes.name: Operationalizing biological interpretability in health-related visual stimuli using multimodal artificial intelligence as standardized non-human raters
nodes.venue: Scientific Reports
nodes.abstract: Abstract Evaluation and assessment research in health communication requires structured, construct-based approaches for interpreting visual materials. This study introduces the Asclepius Biological Interpretability Scale, developed through a two-stage modified Delphi process (a joint image-and-item panel followed by an independent item-only panel) grounded in the Biopsychosocial Model and Visual Literacy Theory, and examines whether multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) systems can reproducibly apply this framework relative to internally generated human reference scores. Six artworks (four health-themed and two controls) were evaluated by three multimodal AI models and four researchers (internal human reference) using a standardized protocol with independent researcher-operated accounts, memory-isolation procedures, repeated assessments over two days, and the final 20-item scale. Because Image Type varied across only six stimuli, health-themed versus control differences were summarized at the image level (Cohen’s d), human–AI differences were summarized descriptively at the rater level, and reproducibility was assessed using intraclass correlation coefficients (ICC) and Spearman correlations. Within this development image set, AI-generated scores were descriptively higher for health-themed than for control images on the three biomedical subscales (image-level Cohen’s d = 0.91–1.38) but not on Non-Medical Interpretability (d = 0.49); with four health-themed and two control images, these differences were not statistically significant ( p = 0.19–0.60). Reproducibility across researcher-operated accounts was excellent for the three biomedical subscales (ICC = 0.90–0.97) and moderate for Non-Medical Interpretability (ICC = 0.57), whereas agreement across assessment days was poor (ICC = 0.04–0.46). The four researchers’ internal reference scores were higher than the AI-generated scores on the biomedical subscales for health-themed images (mean differences 1.41–1.96 points) and lower on Non-Medical Interpretability (− 2.02 to − 2.19 points). These findings provide preliminary methodological evidence that multimodal AI can reproducibly apply a structured interpretability framework to controlled visual stimuli. Although day-to-day stability and the Non-Medical Interpretability subscale, which showed substantial internal-consistency problems, require further refinement, the results support the feasibility of using AI as standardized non-human raters within controlled methodological settings. Broader validation using authentic health communication materials and independent external human raters remains necessary.

nodes.name: Near-Real-Time Wildfire Segmentation and Brightness Temperature Estimation from Geostationary Satellite Imagery Using Deep Learning
nodes.venue: Fire
nodes.abstract: Near-real-time wildfire monitoring is essential for situational awareness and emergency response. The Geostationary Operational Environmental Satellite (GOES) observes at 2 km every 5 min, whereas the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS) observes at 375 m twice daily, leaving neither sensor able to track rapidly evolving fires in fine spatial detail. This study introduces a two-step deep learning approach that statistically infers VIIRS-like sub-pixel fire segmentation and brightness temperature (BT) from GOES imagery. The dataset comprises 257 U.S. wildfires within preselected regions of interest, pairing multi-spectral GOES imagery with VIIRS-derived references in four classes (Non-Fire, Small, Medium, and Large) defined by the number of fire pixels. Against an autoencoder-based baseline, the proposed method raises average precision from 0.105 to 0.368 and reduces the fire region BT root mean square error by 72.1% from 81.33 K to 22.69 K. Omission error rates fall from 9.41% to 1.96% for Medium fires and remain at zero for Large fires, whereas Small fires, 37% of the test set, remain at 39.91%. The false positive rate on Non-Fire images falls from 66.86% to 8.48%, near the operational GOES product’s 6.36% with lower omission (31.40% versus 40.35%). Inference completes within 5 min of observation for a monitored region.

nodes.name: Multi-Source Remote Sensing Fusion and Deep Learning for Intelligent Precision Agriculture
nodes.venue: Sensors
nodes.abstract: The fusion of multi-source remote sensing data and deep learning technology has been increasingly applied in precision agriculture. This review focuses on the perception–decision–execution framework and summarizes the current application status, technical routes, and development trends of multi-source remote sensing data fusion and deep learning in precision agriculture. It examines the complementary advantages of multimodal data such as optical, thermal infrared (TIR), Light Detection and Ranging (LiDAR), and synthetic aperture radar (SAR) in characterizing crop physiological traits and structural characteristics. At the algorithmic level, this review analyzes the evolution of deep learning architectures from single convolutional neural networks (CNNs) to spatiotemporal fusion networks (STFNs), Transformer-based architectures, and emerging state-space models, with emphasis on their capabilities for heterogeneous feature extraction and cross-modal information integration. This review discusses the transformation mechanism from intelligent perception to executable decision-making and explores the application effectiveness of prescription maps and variable-rate task technology in improving resource utilization. This review proposes forward-looking views on core bottlenecks such as model generalization, physical interpretability, and edge computing. This review not only provides a theoretical analysis of precision agriculture but also provides academic recommendations for the development of intelligent agricultural equipment in the future.

nodes.name: Mapping Fuel Categories in Mediterranean Regions with Sentinel-2 and PlanetScope Satellite Acquisitions
nodes.venue: The International Archives of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
nodes.abstract: Accurate and spatially explicit mapping of forest fuel types is essential for developing integrated wildfire risk management strategies, estimating fire danger, and modeling fire propagation in fire-prone Mediterranean ecosystems. While time series of Copernicus Sentinel-2 multispectral imagery at 10 m spatial resolution have proven effective for regional fuel mapping, severe spectral and spatial ambiguities persist in distinguishing complex canopy structures, heterogeneous shrublands, and pastures. This study explores the synergistic integration of Sentinel-2 time series and high-resolution PlanetScope satellite acquisitions (3 m spatial resolution) to produce a 10 m fuel type map (9 classes) over a pilot area in Sardinia, Italy. A total of 114 features were synthesized, combining dynamic Sentinel-2 metrics (kNDVI, FAPAR, NDMI, ReNDVI harmonics), PlanetScope seasonal kNDVI zonal statistics and Gray-Level Co-occurrence Matrix (GLCM) textural features, and static terrain/canopy parameters. Using an XGBoost machine learning classifier trained on 245 photo-interpreted Regions of Interest (80/20 spatial split), three sets of features were compared. The combined model achieved a test overall accuracy of 74.46%, compared to 74.05% for Sentinel-2 alone and 74.66% for PlanetScope alone. Notably, incorporating PlanetScope textural features significantly improved classification metrics for dense canopy classes, increasing the F1-score of broadleaf evergreen trees and needleleaf evergreen trees. The PlanetScope GLCM kNDVI autumn entropy emerged as the most important feature overall. Conversely, PlanetScope performed poorly on the grass class. These findings highlight the critical trade-offs and high complementarity between fine spatial texture and broad spectral coverage for operational wildfire management.

LINGUAGEM MULTIMODAL NA EDUCAÇÃO: CONTRIBUIÇÕES DE DIFERENTES FORMAS DE REPRESENTAÇÃO PARA A APRENDIZAGEM SIGNIFICATIVA
nodes.venue: Diálogos e Construções Acadêmicas do Conhecimento Educacional
nodes.abstract: A linguagem multimodal tem adquirido crescente relevância no campo educacional por possibilitar a articulação de diferentes formas de representação na construção e comunicação do conhecimento. Este estudo teve como objetivo analisar as contribuições da linguagem multimodal para a aprendizagem significativa, considerando o papel de recursos linguísticos, visuais, gráficos, gestuais e digitais em diferentes contextos educacionais. Trata-se de uma revisão integrativa da literatura, realizada a partir de estudos publicados entre 2021 e 2026, nos idiomas português e inglês, mediante buscas nas bases Springer, Miguilim, SUDOC, DOAJ, Latindex e repositórios de periódicos vinculados ao OJS. Foram analisadas publicações relacionadas à multimodalidade, representação do conhecimento, letramento multimodal, práticas pedagógicas e processos de aprendizagem. Os resultados evidenciaram que a integração entre diferentes modos semióticos pode favorecer a elaboração conceitual, a comunicação de conhecimentos, a participação dos estudantes e o desenvolvimento de competências linguísticas, científicas, visuais e digitais. Verificou-se, entretanto, que a simples utilização de múltiplos recursos não assegura aprendizagem significativa, sendo necessária sua articulação intencional aos objetivos pedagógicos, às características dos estudantes e à complexidade dos conteúdos. Conclui-se que a linguagem multimodal constitui recurso relevante para diversificar experiências educativas e ampliar possibilidades de construção do conhecimento.

Joint detection and state recognition of traffic lights and signs through a lightweight hybrid CNN–transformer framework
nodes.venue: Discover Robotics
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate detection of traffic lights and signs is a critical task for safe autonomous vehicle systems (AVS). Despite advances in deep learning, most methods treat traffic light detection, traffic sign detection, and state recognition as separate tasks, while CNN-based models lack global context modeling and transformer-based approaches incur high computational cost. To address these limitations, this study presents a unified and lightweight YOLOv11–EfficientViT framework that jointly performs traffic light detection, traffic sign detection, and traffic light state recognition within a single end-to-end architecture. The proposed method integrates convolutional block attention modules (CBAM) into the YOLOv11 backbone for enhanced local feature refinement and incorporates an efficient vision transformer (EfficientViT) module to capture global contextual dependencies with reduced computational cost. A multi-task loss formulation is adopted to simultaneously optimize localization and semantic state recognition. Experiments were conducted on curated, task-focused subset of BDD100K dataset for traffic light detection and state recognition and TT100K dataset for traffic sign detection. On BDD100K, the proposed model achieved 99.4% mean average precision (mAP@0.5), 92.2% mAP@[0.5:0.95], and 97.7% traffic light state recognition accuracy under the defined experimental setting while maintaining inference at 3.8 ms per frame. On TT100K, the framework attained 96.5% mAP@0.5 and 81.2% mAP@[0.5:0.95] with only 2.5M parameters. Cross-dataset evaluation on subsets of LISA and Bosch datasets further indicates promising cross-dataset transferability with limited performance variation under domain shift. The results indicate that the hybrid integration of attention-enhanced convolutional features and lightweight transformer-based global reasoning enhances detection performance and semantic consistency without compromising computational efficiency.

nodes.name: IoT-Enabled Instrumentation Architectures for Predictive Maintenance and Remote Monitoring in Large-Scale Automated Industrial Plants
nodes.venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
nodes.abstract: The fast industrial digitalization process results in the implementation of Internet of Things (IoT) technologies into the big automated plants to improve its operational precision, reliability, and sustainability. The paper presents a novel IoT-based instrumentation architecture to predictive maintenance and remote monitoring in the scale of industrial setup. The suggested architecture combines distributed smart sensors, edge computing nodes, industrial communication systems, cloud-based analytics systems, and machine-learning models so that they can be used to monitor assets health in real-time and detect early faults. The system reduces system downtime occurrence and minimizes maintenance expenses by making use of condition-based monitoring, anomaly detection and time-series based predictive modeling. The architecture allows deploying the large-scale distribution with geographically distributed plants, as well as provides interoperability with previous industrial control systems like SCADA, and based on PLC infrastructures. The hybrid edge-cloud data processing model is offered to decrease the latency and to manage bandwidth overheads. Simulated large-scale industrial operational conditions show that using the experimental outcome provides remarkable advancements in fault detection, maintenance schedule Optimization and Equipment Effectiveness in general (OEE). Nonetheless, the facts on the ground, like cyber vulnerability threats, inadequate sensor reliability, high entry upfront costs, insufficiency in data control and network delays, continue to be major impediments to full industrialization. Possible directions of future research are the incorporation of digital twins, federated learning in decentralized predictive modeling, the use of AI to calibrate adaptive instrumentation based on upcoming needs, blockchain-based secure data exchange, and 5G-based ultra-reliable and low-latency communication in industrial processes that are mission-critical.

nodes.name: Improving on the spatial location of geostationary satellite-derived FRP by accounting for parallax effect
nodes.venue: The International Archives of the Photogrammetry, Remote Sensing and Spatial Information Sciences
nodes.abstract: When a satellite observes the Earth at an angle, the apparent position of elevated features, such as mountains, clouds or fires in high terrain, can be shifted from their true ground location. This effect, which may be particularly pronounced in the case of geostationary platforms providing observations under systematically high viewing angles in many places, is known as parallax displacement and becomes larger as terrain elevation and satellite viewing angle increase.Meteosat satellites operated by EUMETSAT provide frequent near-real-time observations that are essential for wildfire detection and monitoring. The new Meteosat Third Generation (MTG) satellites, equipped with the Flexible Combined Imager (FCI), offer improved spatial, temporal and spectral capabilities compared with previous systems. These improvements support better detection and tracking of active fires.The LSA SAF Fire Radiative Power product (FRP-PIXEL) provides information on the location, timing and radiative energy of active fires, which can be used as an indicator of fire intensity and biomass consumption. However, standard geostationary processing assumes that observed features are located at sea level. As a result, fires occurring in elevated terrain may be incorrectly geolocated due to parallax displacement.This work presents an updated MTG FRP-PIXEL product that includes both the original fire and terrain-corrected coordinates. The correction aims to improve the spatial accuracy of active-fire locations, especially in mountainous regions. Preliminary comparisons with active-fire information derived from high-resolution Sentinel-2 imagery show that the correction can improve the location of FRP detections over high-elevation terrain.

nodes.name: High-Resolution Burned Area Mapping Using Sentinel-2 Imagery and Robust Satellite Techniques
nodes.venue: Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: High accuracy in burned area (BA) mapping is desirable for many fire-related applications. Most operational products are based on coarse-resolution satellite data with a final spatial resolution ranging from 250 m to 1000 m. The use of higher-resolution satellite data, such as that from the Multispectral Imager (MSI) on board Sentinel-2, is usually reserved for generating BA products only for specific countries and time periods. Moreover, BA algorithms are typically driven by fire detection products to minimize false identifications. The resulting accuracy of such BA products depends strongly on land cover, fire regime, and the reliability of the considered fire detection products. In this paper, we exploit the multitemporal Robust Satellite Technique (RST) to identify burned areas and implement a workflow based on Sentinel-2 images within Google Earth Engine. Test results from two complete region-wide experiments conducted under contrasting seasonal, phenological, and agricultural conditions showed that 97.85% of the mapped area was confirmed as burned within the adopted multi-source validation framework, with an area-based commission error of 1.38% and omission error of 0.60%. Missed detections documented by the Regional Spatial Data Infrastructure (RSDI) amounted to 10.60 ha, corresponding to approximately 0.9% of the burned area reported by RSDI over the tested periods. Polygon-level intercomparison with RSDI and the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS) yielded Intersection over Union (IoU) values of 0.69 and 0.83, respectively. The proposed approach mapped larger burned areas than those reported by both RSDI (+48%) and EFFIS (+143%) as well.

nodes.name: GeCoM: Joint Generative and Interactive Contrastive Self-Supervised Learning for Few-Shot Classification of Multi-Source Remote Sensing Imagery
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Accurate image classification under extreme label scarcity remains a critical challenge in remote sensing, where hyperspectral imagery offers rich spectral signatures but suffers from coarse spatial resolution limitations. Although integrating complementary panchromatic and multispectral data can alleviate this spatial bottleneck, existing methods struggle to fully exploit their deep spatial–spectral features without dense annotations. We propose GeCoM, a joint generative and interactive contrastive self-supervised learning framework for few-shot multi-source image classification. GeCoM employs modality-specific Transformer encoders with a multi-scale masking strategy to reconstruct fine spatial–spectral patterns. Simultaneously, an interactive contrastive optimization module is introduced to align heterogeneous multi-source features within a unified latent space. Experiments on the Houston 2018 benchmark and two regional scenes from Gaofen-14 satellite demonstrate that GeCoM achieves superior Overall Accuracies of 74.66%, 92.36%, and 94.02% with only 15 labeled samples per class, outperforming state-of-the-art baselines. This study provides a robust, label-efficient spatial–spectral representation solution for multi-sensor earth observation.

nodes.name: GSD-Conditioned Generalization of UAV-Trained Oriented Vehicle Detectors Toward Satellite-Relevant Spatial Sampling
nodes.venue: Drones
nodes.abstract: This study examines how train–test ground sampling distance (GSD) mismatch affects UAV-based oriented vehicle detection under controlled source-scene and network-input conditions. Five datasets at 10, 15, 20, 25, and 30 cm/pixel were generated by direct downsampling from the same 1509 UAV source frames while preserving vehicle annotations and data-partition assignments. The GSD conversion procedure was empirically evaluated using 25 image measurements, yielding an overall mean absolute error of 0.180 cm/pixel, root mean square error of 0.225 cm/pixel, and mean absolute relative error of 0.891%. YOLO11m-OBB models were trained under two augmentation settings and three random seeds. The best validation checkpoint from each of 30 training runs was evaluated across all five test GSDs, producing 150 primary cross-GSD evaluations. Mean matched and mismatched AP50−95 were 0.7749 and 0.4915 under controlled augmentation and 0.8166 and 0.7346 under default augmentation, respectively. Across the five equally weighted test GSDs, 15 cm/pixel training achieved the highest mean AP50−95 reaching 0.6249 ± 0.0026 and 0.8049 ± 0.0018 under controlled and default augmentation. For 15-to-30 cm/pixel transfer, recall at a confidence of 0.25 increased from 0.5967 to 0.8407 with default augmentation. Nevertheless, recall remained only 0.0495 for vehicles with an OBB short side below 2 pixels under matched 30 cm/pixel evaluation. These results show that cross-GSD performance depends on augmentation, relative sampling, and object pixel footprint. The findings are limited to the UAV-resampling conditions evaluated here and do not establish a universal optimal GSD or direct transfer to actual satellite imagery.

nodes.name: Fusion-DeepRSM for Satellite-Derived PM2.5 Estimation and Precursor Sensitivity Prediction
nodes.venue: Environmental Science & Technology
nodes.abstract: Abstract Accurate estimation of fine particulate matter (PM2.5) and characterization of precursor-response relationships are crucial for human health protection and air quality management. However, current approaches remain limited by the high computational cost and uncertainties of chemical transport models (CTMs), as well as the sample imbalance and limited interpretability of observation-based machine learning methods. Here, we developed Fusion-DeepRSM, an observation-constrained extension of the Deep Learning Response Surface Model (DeepRSM) framework that integrates CTM simulations, multisource satellite observations, and ground-based measurements to derive spatially continuous PM2.5 concentrations and characterize precursor-PM2.5 response relationships. Results from ground-based observations and CTM-based testbed experiments show that Fusion-DeepRSM effectively alleviates the sample imbalance in conventional models and mitigates PM2.5 overestimation in rural regions, with an average reduction of 4.13 μg/m3 while maintaining high predictive accuracy (R2 = 0.872 and RMSE = 11.82 μg/m3). In addition, Fusion-DeepRSM successfully quantifies precursor-PM2.5 response relationships, revealing pronounced seasonal and regional heterogeneity consistent with established atmospheric chemistry understanding. With high computational efficiency, Fusion-DeepRSM further quantifies the effects of meteorological conditions and pollutant concentrations on PM2.5 variability. During the nationwide PM2.5 decline from 2020 to 2023, unfavorable meteorology partially offset pollutant-related improvements (+1.2 versus −1.8 μg/m3), while changes in precursor pollutant conditions played an important role in the February 2023 PM2.5 rebound in the Beijing–Tianjin–Hebei region. These findings demonstrate the strong potential of Fusion-DeepRSM for air quality modeling and region-specific pollution mitigation.

nodes.name: Few-shot class-incremental SAR target recognition via multi-task representation learning network with structural knowledge distillation
nodes.venue: Journal of Applied Remote Sensing
nodes.abstract: In recent years, significant progress has been made in class-incremental synthetic aperture radar (SAR) automatic target recognition (ATR). However, existing methods heavily rely on large-scale labeled data, which is impractical for real-world incremental scenarios where new classes emerge with limited samples. This scarcity of new-class data brings about dual challenges during class incremental learning: catastrophic forgetting of old classes and severe overfitting of new classes. To tackle these challenges, we propose a few-shot class-incremental ATR method called multi-task representation learning network with structural knowledge distillation, which effectively balances the dilemma of stability and plasticity of the model. Concretely, we develop a multi-task representation learning network to learn class-agnostic representation and strengthen the class decision boundaries under the paradigm of self-supervised learning and supervised learning at base sessions, which is very beneficial for the recognition model to generalize to new classes while maintaining the separation of the base classes. To alleviate the problem of catastrophic forgetting on old classes during class-incremental learning, we present a structural knowledge distillation-based knowledge recall strategy, which leverages the angular invariance among different features to constrain the drift of the intra-class structural relationship before and after the incremental update of the recognition model. Evaluation experiments on three publicly available SAR datasets illustrate that the proposed method is competitive with many state-of-the-art methods.

nodes.name: Factor Graph-Based Geomagnetic SLAM Approach for Smartphone-Based Indoor Localization
nodes.venue: Electronics
nodes.abstract: Indoor geomagnetic positioning provides a low-cost solution for smartphone-based localization without requiring additional infrastructure. However, conventional geomagnetic positioning methods depend on labor-intensive offline magnetic data surveys, limiting deployment flexibility. To address this problem, this paper proposes a factor graph-based geomagnetic SLAM method combining confidence-aware loop closure detection with local–global collaborative optimization. A Gaussian process regression (GPR)-based magnetic model is constructed from measured step-level magnetic observations, and a window-based particle filter integrates magnetic sequence matching with pedestrian dead reckoning (PDR). Confidence-aware loop detection combines magnetic sequence similarity with PDR-derived geometric verification, while continuous confidence weights regulate the influence of accepted associations on back-end optimization. Factor graph-based local–global collaborative optimization coordinates trajectory correction with GPR map refinement to support simultaneous mapping and localization. Cross-user experiments involving three participants yielded mean localization errors of 1.19–1.31 m and RMSEs of 1.35–1.45 m. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework reduces accumulated trajectory drift while supporting online geomagnetic mapping.

nodes.name: Facial Expression-based Music Recommendation using Fourier Image Transformer
nodes.venue: International Journal of Engineering Trends and Technology
nodes.abstract: The ability to recognize human facial expressions is a fundamental requirement for developing advanced human–computer interaction systems. Humans convey emotions primarily through facial expressions, which has driven the development of Facial Expression Recognition (FER) technology in areas such as affective computing and personalized recommendation systems. By leveraging FER, systems can continuously monitor changes in a user’s emotional state throughout the day and generate context-aware responses, thereby enhancing overall user experience. The Spotify application of FER is a music recommendation, where songs are suggested based on facial expressions to match or influence the user’s emotions. Traditional FER approaches primarily rely on spatial-domain features, which often struggle to capture global context and subtle frequency-based patterns in facial images. To address these limitations, this study introduces the Fourier Image Transformer (FIT), a frequency-domain transformer model capable of learning discriminative global representations of facial expressions. By transforming facial images into the frequency domain, FIT captures both local and global variations in facial patterns, improving recognition accuracy and robustness. The proposed framework is trained and tested on the Real-world Affective Faces Multi-Label (RAF-ML) dataset and FER2013, which contains diverse real-world facial expressions under varying conditions. The preprocessing steps, including face detection, image enhancement, resizing, and normalization, to ensure reliable feature extraction. Recognized FER are subsequently mapped to selected music tracks, enabling personalized and image-based music recommendation. This approach offers a seamless, non-intrusive interface that adapts to user emotions in real-time. The FIT model achieved outstanding performance with an accuracy of 98.97%, precision of 98.92%, recall of 98.87%, and an F1-score of 98.90%. The study demonstrates how frequency-domain transformers can enhance FER performance and support intelligent, emotion-driven applications.

nodes.name: Exploring residents’ well-being factors on the Multilevel Model of Healthcare Professional (HCP): Insight from the nationwide cross-sectional survey
nodes.abstract: Abstract Background Resident well-being is shaped by factors extending beyond individual distress, including interpersonal relationships, training structures, organisational conditions, and the wider health-care system. Empirical applications of integrated multilevel frameworks to resident well-being remain limited. We applied the Multilevel Model of Healthcare Professional Well-Being to describe resident well-being in South Korea before the 2024 workforce crisis and to examine differences by postgraduate year (PGY) and specialty track. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional secondary analysis of the 2020 Korean Physician Survey, a nationwide online survey administered by the Korean Medical Association. The analytic sample included 650 residents in PGY1–4. Two medical-education faculty mapped survey items to five levels of well-being (individual, interpersonal, training-program, organisational, and system), and five faculty experts evaluated the appropriateness of level classification and item relevance. We compared retained item-level indicators across PGY groups using one-way analysis of variance or Welch’s analysis of variance, with post-hoc comparisons where appropriate. Essential and non-essential specialty tracks were compared using independent-samples t-tests or Welch’s t-tests. Results The final framework comprised 48 indicators across the five levels. Differences by PGY were most evident in organisational conditions and selected individual-level indicators. Compared with senior residents, junior residents reported longer working hours, fewer days off, lower satisfaction with working hours, shorter sleep duration, lower self-rated health, and higher perceived stress. Burnout and emotional labour did not differ significantly across PGY groups. Residents in essential specialties reported less favourable organisational conditions than those in non-essential specialties, including longer weekday, weekend, and public-holiday working hours; fewer annual days off; and lower satisfaction with working hours, typical workload, and the availability of medical resources. They also devoted a greater proportion of their workload to clinical practice (81.4% vs 68.9%) and reported lower leisure-time and life satisfaction, shorter sleep duration, higher perceived stress, and lower satisfaction with the overall health-care system. Burnout did not differ significantly by specialty track. Conclusions Resident well-being was heterogeneous across postgraduate years and specialty tracks, particularly with respect to organisational conditions. The absence of differences in burnout did not indicate uniform well-being across resident groups. A multilevel assessment that incorporates individual experiences alongside training-program, organisational, specialty-specific, and system-level conditions may provide a more complete basis for understanding and improving resident well-being. Longitudinal studies using resident-specific validated measures are needed to assess changes over time and clarify the relationships between training conditions and well-being.

nodes.name: Explainable Machine Learning Combined with Feature Selection and Bayesian Optimization for Predicting Rare Earth Elements and Yttrium in Coal: A Case Study of China’s Five Major Coal-Bearing Regions
nodes.venue: Energy & Fuels
nodes.abstract: Abstract Determining the concentrations of rare earth elements and yttrium (REY) in coal is essential for evaluating coal-hosted critical metal resources and understanding their geochemical controls. However, conventional laboratory analyses are costly, time-consuming, and spatially sparse, limiting regional-scale assessment. In this study, we compiled 527 coal samples from 30 coalfields across China’s five major coal-bearing regions and developed an explainable machine learning framework for REY prediction. Unlike previous site-specific models, this framework integrates feature selection, Bayesian optimization, and SHAP interpretation for REY prediction at a broad regional scale. After data preprocessing, multicollinearity diagnosis, and correlation-based feature selection, 16 predictors were retained for model construction. Four ensemble regression models, including Random Forest (RF), Extra Trees (ET), CatBoost (CAT), and Gradient Boosting Decision Tree (GBDT), were optimized using Bayesian hyperparameter search and 5-fold cross-validation. The ET model achieved the best test-set performance among the four ensemble models, with RMSE = 39.962, MAE = 29.669, and R2 = 0.716, although predictions for highly enriched samples remained uncertain because of the long-tailed REY distribution. SHAP analysis identified Ga as the most influential predictor, followed by geological age and P2O5, suggesting that clay-related terrigenous input, stratigraphic context, and minor phosphate-associated phases may jointly influence model-predicted REY enrichment. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework can serve as an effective prescreening tool to prioritize coal samples for detailed REY analysis, while independent validation is recommended for high-value target areas.

nodes.name: Enhancing Lithological Interpretation: An Integrated Machine Learning Approach for Automated Log Classification in Volcanic Geothermal Reservoirs, Japan
nodes.venue: SPE Asia Pacific Oil & Gas Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Japan's volcanic geothermal reservoirs present significant subsurface characterization challenges due to complex lithological heterogeneity, extensive faulting, and fracture-controlled permeability. Conventional lithological evaluation often relies on adequate wireline and logging-while-drilling (LWD) measurements, drilling cuttings and expert borehole image interpretation. However, the logging variety is often limited, and drilling cuttings recovery is frequently poor or absent within productive geothermal feed zones because of severe mud losses. As a result, critical information is unavailable where accurate reservoir characterization is most needed. This study presents an integrated machine learning workflow for automated lithofacies classification using borehole image data. The methodology combines unsupervised and supervised learning within a two-stage framework. In the first stage, key geological attributes, including high-frequency resistivity, boundary dip trend, and fracture density, are extracted from borehole images and used as inputs to an Index Probabilized Self-Organized Mapping (IPSOM) workflow (Leon et al., 2015). The resulting clusters are calibrated using geological interpretation and drilling cuttings information to establish lithofacies classes. In the second stage, these calibrated lithofacies labels are used to train a supervised deep learning model that directly predicts lithofacies from borehole images. In this study, the IPSOM workflow successfully differentiated major volcanic lithofacies, including fractured andesite tuff and highly fractured dacite tuff intervals. The supervised model achieved a validation F1 score of 79%, demonstrating its ability to learn lithofacies characteristics from borehole image data. Application to blind test intervals showed promising performance in identifying highly fractured dacite tuff associated with permeable fluid-flow pathways. By integrating geological expertise with machine learning, the workflow reduced interpretation time from approximately one month to 4–6 hours while maintaining geological consistency. The methodology provides a scalable framework for rapid lithofacies characterization and supports more efficient geothermal reservoir evaluation and development.

Enhanced crop yield estimation in smart agriculture via AI and IoT using the GODL geo-optimized algorithm
nodes.venue: Peer-to-Peer Networking and Applications
nodes.abstract: Abstract Precision agriculture is one of the major breakthroughs which has been adopted to counteract some of the major challenges facing contemporary agriculture, such as maximizing crop yield, maximizing resource efficiency, and sustainability. The application of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and the Internet of Things (IoT) technologies can go a long way in enhancing crop yield prediction through data obtained from multiple sources, including satellite images, ground sensors, and weather stations. This research paper proposes a next-generation crop yield prediction system called Geo-Optimized Deep Learning (GODL) algorithm. The GODL algorithm integrates geospatial information with deep learning algorithms for crop yield analysis and prediction. This combination of deep learning and geospatial data allows accurate and scalable crop yield predictions using geospatial and sensor information. In order to ensure model optimization in terms of accuracy and efficiency, the GODL Algorithm makes use of advanced hyperparameter optimization methods that include Adam and Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD). The research paper highlights the efficiency of the GODL Algorithm by conducting extensive experiments that compare the algorithm’s performance with other crop yield prediction models like Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) and other machine learning techniques. The evaluation takes into consideration important metrics such as accuracy, Jaccard Index, Fowlkes-Mallows Index (FMI), and G-mean, as well as IoT data delay and its effects on the prediction accuracy. In future research, the use of blockchain technology to facilitate data sharing and edge computing to process the data will be considered.

nodes.name: Design and Control of an Intelligent Mobile Gardening Robot Supported by Deep Learning-Based Image Processing
nodes.venue: Tarım Bilimleri Dergisi
nodes.abstract: In this study, the design and control of a mobile gardening robot based on image processing and artificial intelligence were implemented. The system, running on Raspberry Pi 4B, can distinguish different plant species and weeds using a YOLOv5-based object detection and classification model; it performs tasks such as cutting weeds, watering useful plants, and moving autonomously while avoiding obstacles. Experiments conducted in a pot environment demonstrated that the robot can successfully perform plant detection, classification, and maintenance functions. With these features, the developed robot offers a low-cost and sustainable solution for small and medium-scale agricultural businesses. The mobile gardening robot designed within the scope of the study was experimentally tested for image processing-based plant recognition, autonomous plant orientation, plant cutting, and watering operations for different scenarios. When the results obtained were examined, it was seen that the developed deep learning-based plant detection model achieved an 82% mAP@50 success rate, while the plant classification model achieved a 92.9% mAP@50 success rate.

nodes.name: Cross-Domain Adaptive Drilling Optimization for Cold-Start Deep Formations in Iraq: A Domain-Adversarial Transfer Framework
nodes.venue: SPE Asia Pacific Oil & Gas Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract In central Iraq, Oilfield A has a shallow drilling history but no prior target-well data for the planned deep interval. The approximately 3,446–4,164-m section targets Formation Z, with Formation R retained as the lower planning boundary. Oilfield B, approximately 130 km away, provides audited deep-well records, but geological, well-profile, bit, bottomhole-assembly, and operating-range shifts create risks of negative transfer and unsupported control actions. Because AZ-1 remains a planned well, this study establishes a pre-deployment cross-field workflow aimed at improving low-delay predictive adaptation and preserving action safety and executability under field limits. The workflow combines a domain-adversarial neural network encoder with a twin-delayed deep deterministic policy gradient controller. Candidate actions are subject to explicit rate limits of 15 kN per update for weight on bit (WOB) and 10 rev/min per update for surface rotary speed. Six Oilfield B Formation Z branches are treated as pseudo-targets in complete-branch, forward-only replay, while training, normalization, and domain alignment use only previously drilled intervals. A history-conditioned surrogate predicts rate of penetration (ROP), surface torque, and standpipe pressure. Target observations update residual bias after a 10-m burn-in. Candidate actions then pass engineering, local-support, uncertainty, load-risk, and paired ROP effect gates, with retention of the current setting defined as an admissible control outcome. Separately, a preregistered static-only blind-target projection was generated from the planned AZ-1 design-state sequence at a 60-kN WOB baseline, without using target-response history. The blind-target projection estimated a mean Formation Z ROP of 8.503 m/h, 5.43% above the 75th percentile of the Oilfield B Formation Z ROP distribution, which was 8.065 m/h. This value was retained as a pre-drill benchmark rather than interpreted as achieved drilling uplift. Across 445 pooled 5-m out-of-fold blocks, the surrogate achieved coefficients of determination of 0.763, 0.971, and 0.967 for ROP, surface torque, and standpipe pressure, respectively. At a past-only 1-m observation delay, sequential calibration reduced ROP prediction root-mean-square error by 9.80% relative to direct transfer, with a 95% target-bootstrap interval of 4.73%–14.77% and improvement across all six pseudo-targets. Corresponding reductions were 9.62% for surface torque and 11.40% for standpipe pressure. Under the frozen support definition, all standard TD3 proposals were outside the historical support region. The support-aware control layer rejected unsupported candidates and maintained zero WOB-bound and action-rate violations. Of 1,837 retrospectively screened candidate-state points, 85 reached pre-effect eligibility, but no nonzero WOB action established a positive paired ROP lower bound. The final advisory therefore retained the current setting. The study distinguishes three levels of cold-start evidence: target-specific pre-drill projection, low-delay predictive adaptation after target observations become available, and support-aware control safety and executability. It further separates accurate response prediction from the evidence required to release a drilling action. The resulting workflow provides a quantified pre-deployment path for AZ-1 in which unsupported parameter changes are withheld until local action-effect evidence becomes adequate.

nodes.name: CT Image-Based PCA Reconstruction Residual Analysis for Structural Anomaly Diagnosis of Lithium-Ion Batteries
nodes.venue: World Electric Vehicle Journal
nodes.abstract: Lithium-ion batteries in electric vehicles operate under complex conditions, including frequent charge–discharge cycling, high-power operation, fast charging, temperature variations, and mechanical vibration, which can contribute to progressive internal structural degradation and associated safety risks. However, conventional electrochemical parameters have limited capability to directly characterize localized structural changes inside batteries. To address this issue, a structural anomaly diagnosis method based on principal component analysis (PCA) reconstruction residuals of X-ray computed tomography (CT) projection images is proposed. A cylindrical lithium iron phosphate cell subjected to accelerated high-rate cycling was used for evaluation, and projection images from a fresh cell of the same type were used to construct the PCA normal-structure model. The central region of each projection image was extracted as the region of interest. Pixel-wise squared reconstruction residuals were further analyzed to characterize localized structural deviations. Among the candidate residual-intensity and spatial-distribution features, the most discriminative feature achieved an absolute standardized mean difference of 9.332 between the pre-cycling and 100-cycle feature-evaluation datasets. When the fixed decision rule was applied without model retraining or threshold adjustment, consistent structural-state classification was observed across the angular projection views acquired after 200, 300, and 400 cycles. Sensitivity analysis and comparison with reference methods further supported the robustness of the observed feature separation under the present experimental setting. The proposed method reduces the dependence on complete three-dimensional CT reconstruction and extensive anomalous-sample annotation, demonstrating the feasibility of an interpretable CT-projection-based approach for nondestructive assessment of internal battery structural states.

nodes.name: CO2 Mineralization Reaction-Induced Pore-Structure Evolution and Its Effects on CO2 Sweep Behavior in Shale: Stage-Dependent Causal Discovery and Causality-Informed Machine Learning Assisted by LBM Simulations
nodes.venue: SPE Asia Pacific Oil & Gas Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract CO2 injection in shale oil reservoirs can effectively enhance oil recovery while also facilitating CO2 sequestration. During CO2 mineralization, rock dissolution and the secondary precipitation of supersaturated mineral ions critically govern the evolution of reservoir pore structure and, consequently, CO2 sweep behavior. Therefore, to elucidate the stage-dependent factors controlling CO2 sweep and pore-throat evolution, we combined CO2 mineralization experiments, lattice Boltzmann simulations, causal discovery, and machine-learning prediction.X-ray diffraction (XRD) and confocal laser scanning microscopy (CLSM) were used to characterize shale mineral composition and pore morphology. The extracted pore geometry, mineral attributes, and proportions were incorporated into a previously developed and experimentally validated multi-mineral-informed lattice Boltzmann model to simulate the time-dependent evolution of pore structure and CO2 concentration. A database covering 200,000 LBM time steps was established. Based on characteristic changes in pore-scale parameters, the mineralization process was divided into an early dissolution stage, an intermediate equilibrium stage, and a late precipitation stage. Graphical Lasso and information-geometric causal inference were used to identify stage-specific directed relationships, which were incorporated into a causal-weight transformation for prediction. The cumulative CO2 sweep coefficient increased from 0.006 to 0.326, with increments of 0.098, 0.062, and 0.158 in the three stages, respectively, demonstrating pronounced stage-wise evolution. During the early dissolution stage, maximum pore diameter and surface roughness directly governed CO2 sweep, with normalized weights of 0.641 and 0.359. During the intermediate equilibrium stage, reservoir wettability and reactive mineral fraction became dominant, with weights of 0.502 and 0.498. During the late precipitation stage, wettability, porosity, surface roughness, and reactive mineral fraction jointly controlled sweep behavior, with weights of 0.324, 0.238, 0.220, and 0.219. Reaction-stage partitioning substantially improved prediction, while causal weighting further reduced errors for most models; the MAPE values of KNN-5, second-order polynomial Ridge, random forest, and gradient boosting decreased to 6.71%, 0.62%, 0.35%, and 4.35%, respectively. This work clarifies the stage-dependent causal mechanisms linking mineralization, pore-structure evolution, wettability, and CO2 sweep behavior, providing a physically interpretable framework for predicting CO2-accessible pore ranges during shale oil recovery and geological carbon sequestration.

nodes.name: Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Visual–Inertial Navigation for Autonomous Lunar Surface Mobility: Systems, Datasets, Methods, and Open Challenges
nodes.venue: Aerospace
nodes.abstract: Reliable onboard state estimation plays an important role in autonomous lunar surface mobility, given the lack of conventional global navigation satellite system (GNSS) coverage and the challenges of variable illumination and terrain texture. This review synthesizes model-based, learning-based, and hybrid visual–inertial odometry (VIO) approaches and assesses their relevance to lunar surface operations. The reviewed studies suggest that learned components can improve feature extraction, matching, depth estimation, and measurement confidence in selected datasets and operating conditions. However, representative lunar validation and uncertainty calibration remain limited. Given these limitations, hybrid architectures integrating learned components with explicit model-based estimators offer a comparatively testable design direction. Reduced lunar gravity alone does not render monocular scale unobservable; practical scale–bias performance also depends jointly on motion excitation, inertial quality, visual geometry, calibration, and estimation-window length. Stereo, wheel, crater, and map cues can provide additional metric information but introduce source-specific risks involving calibration, slip, association, and registration. Within the resources surveyed, we found no publicly available flight-derived lunar traverse dataset combining synchronized camera–IMU measurements, independent trajectory ground truth, and onboard timing. Evidence-based priorities include representative lunar validation, uncertainty-aware integration of learned components, consistency monitoring across metric sources, explicit estimator health and fallback mechanisms, and target-hardware resource evaluation.

nodes.name: A Study on the Application of Multimodal MRI Deep Learning in the Early Detection of Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head
nodes.abstract: Abstract Objective: Osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH) is a debilitating disorder that frequently leads to hip joint dysfunction. Early and accurate diagnosis is crucial to improving clinical outcomes. This study aimed to develop a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based detection model using the You Only Look Once (YOLO) deep learning framework for automatic identification of early-stage ONFH, and to systematically evaluate how different MRI modalities affect detection performance and their potential for clinical decision support. Methods: We retrospectively collected MRI data from 253 ONFH patients across two medical centers, including T1-weighted Imaging (T1WI) and T2-weighted Imaging (T2WI) sequences. After standardized preprocessing, the dataset was partitioned into training, validation, and test sets (7:1:2). Two sequential experiments were conducted. Experiment 1 compared six YOLO generations (v3, v5, v8, v10, v11, v13) using single-center T1WI data, with precision (P), recall (R), mean average precision (mAP), and inference speed as primary metrics. Experiment 2 applied the optimal model to single-modality (T1WI or T2WI) and multimodal fused images from both centers, using the same metrics to quantify detection efficacy and validate multicenter robustness. Results: In Experiment 1, YOLO v11 outperformed all other models, achieving a mAP@0.5 of 0.966, a recall of 0.941, and a per-frame inference time of 4.9 ms. In Experiment 2, the multimodal fusion input (T1WI+T2WI) yielded the highest performance across all modalities, with a mAP@0.5 of 0.9637, a recall of 0.9388, and the fastest inference time (3.0 ms), surpassing both T1WI (R=0.9159, 4.9 ms) and T2WI (R=0.9113, 6.0 ms) alone. Conclusion: The proposed YOLO v11 model demonstrates excellent performance in MRI-based ONFH detection, and the multimodal fusion strategy further improves both diagnostic accuracy and computational efficiency. This approach addresses the dual clinical requirements for high precision and real-time processing, offering a practical and objective intelligent tool for early ONFH screening.

nodes.name: A Multi-Stage History Matching Workflow with Multiscale Parameter Updates for Field-Scale Edge-Water Gas Reservoirs
nodes.venue: SPE Asia Pacific Oil & Gas Conference and Exhibition
nodes.abstract: Abstract Reducing reservoir uncertainty is essential for improving the predictive capability of reservoir simulation models. This requires a calibration strategy that effectively combines dynamic production observations with static geological information. In this work, a multistage history matching workflow is developed to sequentially update reservoir properties at different spatial scales for edge-water gas reservoirs. The workflow consists of two sequential calibration stages. First, a population-based optimization algorithm is employed to estimate zone-scale pore-volume multipliers and aquifer strength by matching field-scale shut-in bottom-hole pressure (SBHP), thereby capturing the overall reservoir energy and storage capacity. Subsequently, a streamline-based inversion technique is used to refine grid-scale permeability distributions, enabling improved reproduction of well-scale flowing bottom-hole pressure (FBHP) and cumulative water production (WPT). The methodology is demonstrated using a field-scale reservoir from the Sichuan Basin, China. The calibrated model shows significantly improved agreement with historical observations while preserving the underlying geological framework and providing more reliable predictions of water breakthrough. In addition, streamline-based flow diagnostics derived from the calibrated model offer valuable characterization of residual gas distribution and gas drainage regions, providing practical information for future reservoir development and production management.
